pages.text: Workers mine ores and valuable blocks and carry them home. Blue mineral crystals hold 500 each, 5 a trip; a crystal stands on mineralized earth and cannot be broken — your hand takes a shard.
Vespene is a slow green liquid rising in veins from bedrock. A gas building goes on an outlet; a canister of iron and glass carries it.
A vespene bucket over a stick makes four $(l)vespene torches$(), burning green. Vespene, glass and iron make a $(l)vespene lamp$(), as bright as glowstone.

An empty canister and four buckets of vespene make $(l)vespene fuel$(): 64 smeltings in a furnace (eight coal), and the empty canister comes back. Glass among four mineral shards makes four panes of $(l)mineral glass$(), as strong against blasts as obsidian.

Mineral fields stand by most vespene geysers, and underground lie $(l)mineral halls$(): big caves with a flat floor and glowing lichen, a geyser in the middle and 4 to 7 crystals round it.$(br2)Water on vespene makes cobblestone, as on lava (on an outlet the water turns, not the outlet). A vespene outlet open to the sky slowly grows up into a $(l)volcano$() — a block every 3 minutes, a cobblestone cone round it. A gas building put on a volcano breaks it: the cone and the column go and the building stands at the ground.

Supply comes from overlords, supply depots and pylons. Prices, build times and supply follow StarCraft II. Workers find minerals and geysers within 100 blocks of their store, other valuables within 10 blocks of themselves, walls or not; with nothing in reach they explore the land and the caves. A worker in danger gets an escort, and a dark place is lit its race's way.$(br2)A new base stands on 20 blocks of plain stone under a top of $(l)concrete$() its workers never dig.
